answer.text: point out other ways a tag could reach a neighbouring plant
answer.line: Paragraph 12 says the network is not the only road, lists other routes, then says none requires a fungal conduit.

steps: Read the paragraph's first line. It names the job: the network is not the only road.
List the other roads in sentence 2: soil water, carbon dioxide breathed out and fixed again, fallen litter, root grafts.
Sentence 3 lands it: "none requires a fungal conduit." So a tag in a neighbour may not be network traffic. The list is support, not the topic.

choices.text: argue that soil water supplies most of the nutrients in a forest
choices.note: Soil water is one road a tag can take, not the forest's main nutrient supply.

choices.text: point out other ways a tag could reach a neighbouring plant
choices.note: Sentence 1 sets the job and sentence 3 closes it: other roads, none fungal.

choices.text: explain why root grafts form between trees of the same species
choices.note: Grafts are one item on the list, and why they form is never explained.

choices.text: describe the way fallen leaves decompose on a forest floor
choices.note: Litter is one item on the list; the paragraph never describes how leaves decay.

choices.text: show that the fungal route carries more carbon than the soil route does
choices.note: No amounts are compared: sentence 3 says pulling the routes apart is genuinely difficult, the opposite of ranking them.

lockIt: Function of a paragraph: its first and last lines usually state its job; the middle is support.
